recommendation_summary: The reply's action now is to keep the spreadsheet only as the list of accepted bookings and send every new reservation, from both offices, through a single save. That save locks the item, checks its dates for overlap and refuses the second conflicting submit. It offers no optional extras. It explicitly rejects colour formatting, reminders, an unlocked pre-check and a new booking system. Unmet need: it never says what technology would provide the shared lock-and-check save. It only implies a single shared point where the check is enforced.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The owner requires that a second reservation for the same item and overlapping dates is rejected at save time, including when two agents submit together. You asked whether red conditional formatting and a reminder, shipped this week on the current spreadsheet, is enough.
labels.Deleted: Conditional formatting and a check reminder, because both saves stay stored. A pre-check that does not hold a lock across the save, because both agents can pass it. A new booking system, because it is more than the rule needs.
labels.Bottleneck: The save accepts the overlapping reservation. Colour on the sheet runs only after both rows exist.
labels.Checked myself: Six agents, two offices, one identifier per physical item, and a double booking on overlapping dates last week. I have not opened the spreadsheet.

note: The single locked save with an overlap check and refusal of the second submit is enforced conflict checking that handles simultaneous submits, but it is a borderline pass because the reply never names what would enforce the lock on the server.
